[Topic: Absence Policy]
[Topic: Absence Policy] 1. Excused Absences: An absence is only considered excused if it is due to sickness (supported by a valid medical certificate) or force majeure (calamities/natural disasters). 2. Notification: In case of sickness or unforeseen incidents, the student must inform their immediate supervisor at the host training establishment, the OJT Supervisor/Instructor, and the Team Leader at least one hour before their official start time. 3. Documentation: A medical certificate or relevant documentation must be submitted upon return. 4. Demerits: Unexcused absences reflect poorly on the final evaluation and may incur demerits in the OJT grading system.

[Topic: Ccs Officials]
CCS Department Heads: MR. JOHN D. SAGAPSAPAN, MSIT – Associate Dean, CCS MR. CHARLIE D. BAGUIO, MSIT – Practicum Coordinator, CCS

[Topic: Ccs Overview]
The College of Computing Studies (CCS) offers the Bachelor of Science in Information Systems and the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science programs. Its core focus areas include software development, system analysis, database administration, and IT project management. Practicum and OJT requirements: BSCS requires a minimum of 200 hours of OJT in an IT-related organization. BSIS requires 480 hours. Training is overseen by the Practicum Coordinator and Associate Dean and requires an approved Memorandum of Agreement from the University President.

[Topic: Clearance Procedures]
[Topic: Clearance and Completion Procedures] 1. Narrative Report: Upon completion of the required OJT hours, students must submit a comprehensive Narrative Report documenting their daily activities, learnings, and reflections. 2. Daily Time Record (DTR): All DTRs must be signed by the host company supervisor and submitted for verification of hours completed. 3. Evaluation Forms: Both the Host Training Establishment (HTE) supervisor and the OJT coordinator must complete an evaluation of the student's performance. 4. Final Clearance: Final OJT clearance is granted only after the submission of the Narrative Report, signed DTR, and completed evaluation forms. Students should ensure all deficiencies are cleared before the end of the semester.

[Topic: Competencies]
OJT LEARNING COMPETENCIES AND ACTIVITIES Software Development – Design, create, and maintain software solutions. Machine Learning Engineering – Develop AI algorithms using machine learning techniques. IT-Related Research – Assist research in information technology and applied computing. UX/UI Design – Develop prototypes and layouts for client projects. Information Security Analysis – Monitor networks and support cybersecurity initiatives. Networking – Assist in network configuration, installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance. Technical Support – Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain computer systems. Data Analysis – Collect, process, and interpret organizational data. Customer Service – Communicate and coordinate with clients. Data Entry and Management – Maintain accurate and well-organized database records. Office Work – Perform clerical and administrative tasks.

[Topic: Documents Summary]
Required OJT documents include the Parent’s Waiver and Consent Form, Recommendation Letter for OJT Deployment, Memorandum of Agreement, Letter of Acceptance from the Host Establishment, Medical Certificate and laboratory results, Student Copy from Registrar, Resume and Application Letter, Evaluation Sheet, Certificate of Completion, and Excuse Slip when applicable.

[Topic: Dress Code]
[Topic: Dress Code and Grooming] 1. Proper Grooming: OJT students must observe proper grooming at all times during their practicum. This includes neat hair, clean nails, and overall professional presentation. 2. Attire: Unless a specific uniform is provided by the host training establishment, students should wear appropriate professional or business attire according to industry standards. 3. University Identity: Students should always carry their university ID and, if required, wear the specified OJT uniform or school uniform on designated days. 4. Professionalism: Attire should be modest and reflect the professional standards of Jose Rizal Memorial State University.

[Topic: Dtr Guidelines]
The Daily Time Record is the official attendance log during OJT. It includes the date, morning in and out, afternoon in and out, and the total hours rendered. It must be signed by the supervisor and validated by the OJT Coordinator and compiled in the narrative report appendices.

[Topic: Evaluation Sheet]
This document evaluates trainee performance based on personal traits, intellectual and professional deportment, communication skills, and general performance using a rating scale from outstanding to poor.

[Topic: Excuse Slip]
This document officially excuses students from classes or duties. It contains the student name, date of absence, reason, and parent or guardian signature.

[Topic: History]
JRMSU was established to provide accessible higher education and promote regional development. Over the years, the university expanded its programs and campuses. It is recognized for its commitment to academic quality and holistic human development.

[Topic: Jrmsu Core Values]
Humane Trust Innovative Excellence Transformational Communication

[Topic: Jrmsu Goals]
Goals (GRIPS): G – Globally competitive educational institution R – Resilient to internal and external risks and hazards I – Innovative processes and solutions in research translated to extension P – Partnerships with private enterprise, HEIs, government agencies, alumni S – Sound fiscal management and participatory governance

[Topic: Jrmsu Mission]
Deliver services in research, instruction, production, and extension. Provide advanced professional, technical, and technopreneurial training. Produce highly competent, innovative, and self-renewed individuals.

[Topic: Jrmsu Vision]
A dynamic, inclusive, and regionally-diverse university in Southern Philippines.

[Topic: Late Attendance Policy]
[Topic: Late Attendance Policy] 1. Tardiness and Log-in/out: OJT trainees are required to log in at least 15 minutes before their official start time and log out 15 minutes after their official end time at the industry or school site. 2. Consequences of Tardiness: If a student accumulates excessive minutes of tardiness or multiple instances of being late, they may be required to perform an eight-hour make-up duty. 3. Habitual Tardiness: Habitual tardiness is subject to demerits and may result in a formal meeting with the OJT coordinator.

[Topic: Memorandum Of Agreement]
This is a formal agreement between JRMSU and the host training establishment. It outlines responsibilities such as recommending trainees, conducting orientation, supervising students, maintaining safe working conditions, monitoring attendance, conducting evaluations, and issuing certificates. It includes termination clauses, confidentiality, intellectual property provisions, and signatories.

[Topic: Narrative Report]
The narrative report consists of three chapters. includes the host training establishment profile such as its overview, brief history, logo and meaning, core values, philosophy, vision, mission, goals, and organizational chart. contains training activities which include narrative experiences, weekly progress reports, Daily Time Record, documentation with photos and captions, evaluation sheet, and certificate of completion. presents results and findings such as accomplishments, competencies gained, outputs, and impact on the student’s career. Appendices include registrar documents, certificates, medical documents, parent consent forms, letters of acceptance, application letters, resumes, and the Memorandum of Agreement.

[Topic: Ojt Grading System]
OJT grading components include Weekly Progress Report at 20 percent, Narrative Report at 20 percent, Coordinator Evaluation at 20 percent, and Supervisor Evaluation at 40 percent. The final grade is recorded in the Transcript of Records.

[Topic: Ojt Requirements]
To participate in the On-the-Job Training (OJT) program at JRMSU, students must be enrolled under the College of Computing Studies programs and satisfy the required OJT hours. The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BSCS) requires a minimum of 200 hours of OJT in an IT-related organization, while the Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (BSIS) requires a minimum of 480 hours of OJT in an IT-related organization. Students must identify a suitable Host Training Establishment (HTE) that can provide IT-related work experience and coordinate with the OJT Coordinator for approval. A Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between JRMSU and the host establishment is required and must be approved by the University President. Multiple notarized copies of the MOA are usually prepared. Before deployment, students must secure and submit several requirements, which commonly include a Parent’s Waiver and Consent Form, a Recommendation Letter for OJT deployment issued by the CCS Practicum Coordinator and noted by the Associate Dean, a Letter of Acceptance from the host establishment, a Medical Certificate and required laboratory results, a Student Copy from the Registrar, and the student’s Resume and Application Letter. During the OJT, students must maintain a Daily Time Record (DTR), participate in orientation and training, perform assigned tasks, and later submit a Narrative Report and other required documents for evaluation and completion of the program.

[Topic: Parent’S Waiver And Consent Form]
This document gives consent for student participation in academic activities including OJT. It is issued by the Office of the Dean of Student Affairs and Services. It specifies the student’s details and includes provisions for health protocols, safety reminders, and liability waiver. It must be signed by parents or guardians and notarized.

[Topic: Procedures]
OJT procedures involve identifying a Host Training Establishment, coordinating with the OJT Coordinator, applying to an establishment and securing an approved MOA, preparing notarized copies of the MOA, submitting requirements such as parent consent and medical certificate, beginning OJT with orientation and training, maintaining a Daily Time Record, and submitting a narrative report and attending the practicum culmination.

[Topic: Quality Policy]
JRMSU provides quality training and development to students. It commits to adequate, suitable, and relevant resources, and implements continuous quality management for client satisfaction.

[Topic: Recommendation Letter For Ojt Deployment]
This is issued by the CCS Practicum Coordinator and noted by the Associate Dean. It recommends students for OJT placement and states the required hours for BSIS and BSCS programs. It also contains student names, host agencies, and contact information.

[Topic: Required Hours Details]
[Topic: Required Hours Details] 1. Total Hours: The required number of OJT hours varies by program. Most programs require between 200 to 400 hours of hands-on training. 2. Program Specifics: For example, Bachelor of Science in Accounting Technology requires a minimum of 320 hours. Other programs may range from 240 to 600 hours depending on the curriculum year. 3. Daily Limits: Students are generally expected to follow regular industry hours but should not exceed 10 hours of training in a single day unless specifically permitted by the coordinator and supervisor. 4. Overtime: Excessive overtime should be avoided to prevent fatigue, though some departments allow make-up hours through overtime with prior approval.
